findings.title: Price manipulation via flash loan
findings.description: The oracle uses a single block spot price for liquidation decisions. An attacker can manipulate the price within one transaction block using a flash loan and immediately trigger under-collateralised liquidations.
findings.recommendation: Use a TWAP oracle with a minimum 30-minute window or integrate Chainlink price feeds with staleness checks.

findings.title: No circuit breaker on extreme price moves
findings.description: The contract has no maximum deviation check. A price jump of >50% in one update is silently accepted, enabling oracle poisoning attacks.
findings.recommendation: Add a deviation guard: revert if new price deviates >20% from the rolling median.

findings.title: Admin can update oracle address without timelock
findings.description: setOracle() can be called by the owner at any time with no delay, allowing instant oracle replacement that could front-run user positions.
findings.recommendation: Enforce a 48-hour timelock on oracle address changes via a governor contract.

findings.title: Missing zero-address check in constructor
findings.description: The oracle address passed to the constructor is not validated, allowing accidental deployment with address(0) and bricking the contract.
findings.recommendation: Add require(oracle_ != address(0)) in the constructor.

gasReport.optimizationHint: Eliminate redundant SLOAD calls in the price update loop — potential 12% gas reduction.

findings.title: Event not emitted on emergency withdrawal
findings.description: The emergencyWithdraw() function transfers funds but does not emit an event, making off-chain monitoring difficult.
findings.recommendation: Add an EmergencyWithdrawal(address user, uint256 amount) event and emit it in emergencyWithdraw().

gasReport.optimizationHint: Use custom errors instead of require strings — saves ~200 gas per revert.

findings.title: No replay protection on cross-chain messages
findings.description: Message hashes are not tracked once processed, allowing relayers to replay bridge messages on the destination chain.
findings.recommendation: Track processed message hashes in a mapping and revert on replay.

findings.title: Centralized relayer with no fallback
findings.description: The bridge depends on a single whitelisted relayer. If the relayer goes offline, funds are permanently locked with no rescue path.
findings.recommendation: Add a time-based escape hatch: after 7 days with no relay, allow depositors to self-withdraw.

findings.title: Integer precision loss in fee calculation
findings.description: Fee calculation divides before multiplying, causing small rounding errors that accumulate over many transactions.
findings.recommendation: Multiply before dividing: fee = (amount * feeBps) / 10000.

gasReport.optimizationHint: Batch multiple bridge operations into a single call to amortise L1 blob costs.

findings.title: Unchecked return value from token transfer
findings.description: transferFrom() is called without checking the return value. Non-reverting ERC-20 tokens (e.g. USDT) can silently fail, leaving the contract in an inconsistent state.
findings.recommendation: Use OpenZeppelin SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom() which enforces return value checks.

findings.title: Fee-on-transfer token incompatibility
findings.description: The contract assumes received amount equals transferred amount. Fee-on-transfer tokens will cause accounting mismatches that can be exploited to drain liquidity.
findings.recommendation: Measure actual received amount by comparing balances before and after transfer.

findings.title: No slippage protection on liquidity add
findings.description: addLiquidity() accepts any ratio without minimum amount checks, exposing LPs to sandwich attacks.
findings.recommendation: Add amountAMin and amountBMin parameters to addLiquidity().

gasReport.optimizationHint: Replace multiple storage reads with a single cached local variable inside the swap loop.

findings.title: Dispute resolution relies on single arbiter
findings.description: The arbiter can unilaterally award funds to either party with no appeal mechanism or dispute window.
findings.recommendation: Implement a 3/5 multisig arbiter panel with a 72-hour dispute window before funds are released.

findings.title: No deadline enforcement on deposit phase
findings.description: Buyer can deposit indefinitely without initiating trade, tying up seller's commitment.
findings.recommendation: Add a depositDeadline timestamp after which the escrow auto-cancels.

findings.title: Missing indexed fields in Transfer event
findings.description: The Transfer event lacks indexed parameters, making it expensive to filter by address in off-chain indexers.
findings.recommendation: Add indexed keyword to address fields in the Transfer event signature.

gasReport.optimizationHint: Pack struct fields to fit within 32-byte slots — saves ~3,000 gas per deposit.

findings.title: Mint function has no max supply cap
findings.description: The owner can mint an unlimited number of tokens, creating unlimited inflation risk. No hard cap enforced at the contract level.
findings.recommendation: Define a MAX_SUPPLY constant and assert totalSupply() + amount <= MAX_SUPPLY before minting.

gasReport.optimizationHint: Use ERC20Permit to replace approve + transferFrom with a single gasless permit signature.

findings.title: Stale price oracle window
findings.description: Price feed used in liquidation logic has no staleness check; a delayed oracle could allow under-collateralised loans.
findings.recommendation: Reject oracle values older than a defined heartbeat (e.g. 30 minutes).

gasReport.optimizationHint: Use immutable variables for oracle address — saves ~2,400 gas per call.

findings.title: Reentrancy in withdraw()
findings.description: The withdraw function sends ETH before updating the user balance, allowing a malicious contract to reenter and drain funds.
findings.recommendation: Apply the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern: update state before external calls, or use ReentrancyGuard.

findings.title: Missing access control on setFeeRate()
findings.description: Any address can call setFeeRate(), allowing arbitrary fee manipulation without protocol governance.
findings.recommendation: Add onlyOwner or a governance timelock guard to setFeeRate().

findings.title: Unbounded loop in distributeRewards()
findings.description: The rewards loop iterates over all stakers without a bound, risking out-of-gas on large staker sets.
findings.recommendation: Implement pagination or a pull-based rewards model.

findings.title: Floating pragma
findings.description: Contract uses ^0.8.0 which may compile under future breaking compiler versions.
findings.recommendation: Lock pragma to a specific version, e.g. 0.8.24.

gasReport.optimizationHint: Pack calldata fields — estimated 18% reduction in L1 blob fees.
